options.text: Tailgating/piggybacking (an unauthorized person following an authorized one through a door)

explanation.correct: A mantrap / access-control vestibule allows only one person through at a time via interlocking doors, preventing tailgating or piggybacking into a secure area.

distractors.A: Power surges are handled by electrical protection, not a mantrap.
distractors.B: SQL injection is an application-layer attack unrelated to physical entry.
distractors.C: Phishing is a social-engineering email threat, not a physical access control.

explanation.exam_pattern: Mantrap/vestibule stops tailgating/piggybacking into secure areas (one person at a time).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Physical access controls

questions.stem: To preserve the independence of the IS audit function, the function should report FUNCTIONALLY to:

options.text: The chief information officer (CIO) whose area it audits
The audit committee of the board of directors

explanation.correct: Reporting functionally to the audit committee (board) keeps the audit function organizationally independent of the IT management whose activities it examines.

distractors.A: IT operations is a subject of the audit, not an independent oversight body.
distractors.B: Software development is audited by the function and cannot be its reporting line.
distractors.C: The CIO owns the IT area under audit; reporting to the CIO impairs independence.

explanation.exam_pattern: Audit reports functionally to the audit committee/board - never to the IT management it audits.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Organizational independence and reporting lines

questions.stem: An IS auditor is assigned to audit a highly specialized system that is outside the auditor's technical expertise. What is the BEST course of action?

options.text: Omit the specialized system and report on the rest
Proceed and rely only on management's verbal assurances
Decline to form any conclusion about the system
Engage or consult a qualified subject-matter expert while retaining responsibility for the audit conclusion

explanation.correct: The proficiency standard lets the auditor use a competent expert's work for areas beyond their skill, but the IS auditor still owns and supervises the conclusion.

distractors.A: Scoping out the key system undermines the purpose of the audit.
distractors.B: Verbal assurances are weak evidence and do not address the competence gap.
distractors.C: Declining abandons the objective; the standards provide for using experts instead.

explanation.exam_pattern: Lack a skill? Use a competent expert - but the auditor still owns the conclusion (proficiency/due care).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Proficiency and use of the work of experts

questions.stem: An IS audit concludes that controls are adequate. Which statement BEST reflects the level of assurance the auditor can provide?

options.text: Absolute assurance that no control weakness or error exists
A guarantee that fraud is impossible
Reasonable assurance, because inherent limitations and sampling mean some issues may go undetected

explanation.correct: Because of sampling and the inherent limitations of any audit, the IS auditor provides reasonable - not absolute - assurance.

distractors.A: The audit does provide assurance; it is reasonable rather than none.
distractors.B: Audits cannot provide absolute assurance that every issue has been found.
distractors.C: No audit can guarantee that fraud is impossible.

explanation.exam_pattern: Audits give REASONABLE assurance, not absolute (sampling + inherent limitations).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Reasonable assurance and inherent limitations

questions.stem: Midway through an engagement, management restricts the IS auditor from accessing records needed to complete testing. What should the auditor do?

options.text: Quietly drop the affected tests and issue an unqualified report
Continue and estimate the missing results
Document the scope limitation and communicate it to those charged with governance, assessing its effect on the conclusion

explanation.correct: A scope limitation must be documented and reported to those charged with governance, and its effect on the audit opinion must be considered.

distractors.A: Silently dropping tests and issuing a clean report misrepresents the audit.
distractors.B: Fabricating or estimating missing results is an ethics violation, not evidence.
distractors.D: Accepting a limitation without comment fails the auditor's reporting duty.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scope limitation -> document it, report to governance, and weigh its effect on the opinion.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Scope limitations and reporting

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The susceptibility of a process or account to a material error, assuming NO related internal controls are in place, is called ______ risk.

explanation.correct: Inherent risk is the risk present before controls are considered; the audit risk model then factors in control risk and detection risk.
explanation.exam_pattern: Inherent = risk before controls; control = controls fail; detection = auditor misses it.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Audit risk components (inherent risk)

questions.stem: An IS auditor assesses both inherent risk and control risk for a process as high. To keep overall audit risk at an acceptable level, the auditor should:

options.text: Issue the report without any testing
Ignore detection risk because it cannot be controlled
Reduce the amount of substantive testing
Increase the extent of substantive testing to lower detection risk

explanation.correct: When inherent and control risk are high, the auditor lowers detection risk - the component they control - by performing more or more rigorous substantive testing.

distractors.A: No testing provides no basis for a supported conclusion.
distractors.B: Detection risk is exactly the component the auditor can manage through testing.
distractors.C: Reducing testing raises detection risk and therefore overall audit risk.

explanation.exam_pattern: High inherent + control risk -> lower detection risk by doing MORE substantive testing.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Audit risk model (inherent x control x detection)

questions.stem: Which component of the audit risk model is reduced when an organization designs and operates strong, effective internal controls?

explanation.correct: Effective internal controls reduce control risk - the risk that a material error is not prevented or detected by the organization's own controls.

distractors.A: Business risk is broader and is not a component of the audit risk model.
distractors.B: Detection risk relates to the auditor's own procedures, not the client's controls.
distractors.C: Inherent risk exists regardless of controls and is not reduced by them.

explanation.exam_pattern: Strong internal controls lower CONTROL risk (not inherent, detection, or business risk).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Control risk

questions.stem: What should be the PRIMARY basis for deciding which areas to include in the annual IS audit plan?

options.text: The personal interests of the audit team
The areas that are easiest and quickest to audit
A risk assessment of the organization's auditable universe

explanation.correct: A risk-based plan allocates audit coverage according to a risk assessment of the auditable universe, directing effort where risk is greatest.

distractors.A: Arbitrary ordering ignores risk entirely.
distractors.B: Personal interest is neither objective nor risk-driven.
distractors.C: Auditing by convenience leaves the highest-risk areas potentially uncovered.

explanation.exam_pattern: The annual audit plan is built from a risk assessment of the audit universe.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Risk-based annual audit planning

questions.stem: An IS auditor wants to determine whether a required access-approval control is actually operating. Which type of test is this?

explanation.correct: A compliance test determines whether a control is being applied as designed (operating effectiveness).

distractors.A: A substantive test verifies the integrity/accuracy of data or balances, not whether a control operates.
distractors.C: Penetration testing probes exploitable security weaknesses, not control operation.
distractors.D: Stress testing checks performance under load.

explanation.exam_pattern: Does the CONTROL operate? = compliance test. Is the DATA accurate? = substantive test.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Compliance vs. substantive testing

questions.stem: For a high-volume online transaction system that cannot be interrupted, which technique lets the IS auditor capture and flag selected transactions continuously as they are processed?

options.text: Reviewing printed reports once a year
Shutting the system down to review it offline
An embedded audit module (e.g., SCARF) built into the application

explanation.correct: An embedded audit module - such as a systems control audit review file (SCARF) - is built into the production application to capture and flag transactions continuously, ideal when processing cannot be stopped.

distractors.A: Annual report review is neither continuous nor transaction-level.
distractors.B: A single year-end sample is not continuous and misses interim activity.
distractors.C: Disabling an online production system is not acceptable.

explanation.exam_pattern: Continuous, in-line transaction capture on a non-stop system = embedded audit module (SCARF).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Continuous auditing and embedded audit modules

questions.stem: An IS auditor uses an integrated test facility (ITF), processing test transactions for a fictitious entity within the LIVE production system. What is the auditor's KEY precaution?

options.text: Allow the test transactions to post permanently to prove the system works
Ensure the test transactions are isolated and reversed so they do not corrupt live data or financial totals
Give every user access to the fictitious entity
Run the ITF only after the system is decommissioned

explanation.correct: Because ITF runs test data through the live system, the test transactions must be segregated and backed out so real data and totals are not contaminated.

distractors.A: Leaving test entries posted corrupts real balances.
distractors.C: Broad access to the test entity is unnecessary and risky.
distractors.D: Running ITF on a decommissioned system defeats its purpose of testing live processing.

explanation.exam_pattern: ITF runs test data through the LIVE system -> isolate and reverse the test transactions.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Integrated test facility (ITF)

questions.stem: An IS auditor reprocesses real production data using the auditor's own independently written program and compares the output to the live system's results. This CAAT is known as:

explanation.correct: Parallel simulation uses the auditor's own program on actual production data, comparing its output with the live system to detect processing errors.

distractors.A: A structured walkthrough is a review/discussion, not reprocessing.
distractors.B: The test data method runs the auditor's (often fictitious) data through the client's program - the reverse of this.
distractors.D: CSA is a facilitated self-review by process owners, not reprocessing of data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Auditor's OWN program + REAL data, compared to production = parallel simulation.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — CAATs (parallel simulation)

questions.stem: Which TWO of the following are PREVENTIVE controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: An input edit/validation check that rejects invalid data before it is processed
Reviewing audit logs weekly to spot unauthorized changes
Segregation of duties between authorizing and recording transactions
Restoring data from backup after corruption is discovered

explanation.correct: An edit check that blocks bad data before processing and segregation of duties both stop an undesirable event before it occurs - preventive controls.

distractors.B: Reviewing logs after the fact discovers events that already happened - a detective control.
distractors.D: Restoring from backup after corruption remediates an event - a corrective control.

explanation.exam_pattern: Preventive = stop before (edit checks, SoD); detective = find after (log review); corrective = fix after (restore).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Types of controls (preventive/detective/corrective)

questions.stem: An IS auditor wants to estimate the total dollar value of misstatement in an accounts-payable file. Which sampling approach is MOST appropriate?

explanation.correct: Variable sampling estimates a numeric amount (such as a monetary value or misstatement), which is what this objective requires.

distractors.A: Discovery sampling aims to find at least one critical/fraudulent item, not estimate a total value.
distractors.B: Attribute sampling estimates a rate of occurrence (how often), not a dollar amount.
distractors.D: Stop-or-go sampling is used to minimize sample size when few errors are expected.

explanation.exam_pattern: Estimate an AMOUNT/value = variable sampling; estimate a RATE of occurrence = attribute sampling.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Variable vs. attribute sampling

questions.stem: An IS auditor suspects fraud and wants a sampling method whose goal is to detect at least one instance of an irregularity when the expected occurrence rate is very low. Which method fits BEST?

options.text: Judgmental sampling of the largest items only

explanation.correct: Discovery sampling is designed to surface at least one instance of a critical deviation or fraud when the expected occurrence rate is very low.

distractors.A: Monetary unit sampling targets overstatement in value, not fraud discovery.
distractors.C: Variable sampling estimates monetary values, not the existence of a rare irregularity.
distractors.D: Testing only the largest items can miss small fraudulent transactions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Find at least one rare/fraudulent instance (low expected rate) = discovery sampling.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Discovery sampling

questions.stem: Which sampling approach is designed to avoid excessive sampling by allowing the auditor to stop as early as possible when few or no errors are expected?

explanation.correct: Stop-or-go sampling lets the test end at the earliest justified point, preventing an unnecessarily large sample when the expected error rate is low.

distractors.A: Cluster sampling draws groups of items; it is not about early stopping.
distractors.B: Variable sampling estimates values and does not inherently minimize sample size.
distractors.C: Stratification groups the population by a characteristic; it does not stop testing early.

explanation.exam_pattern: Minimize sample size / stop early when few errors are expected = stop-or-go sampling.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Stop-or-go sampling

questions.stem: Which procedure gives the IS auditor the STRONGEST evidence that an automated control is operating as intended?

options.text: Asking the control owner whether the control works
Re-performing the control and observing the result directly

explanation.correct: Re-performing the control and directly observing the outcome gives the auditor the most reliable, firsthand evidence that it operates.

distractors.A: A self-assessment is management's assertion, not independent evidence.
distractors.B: Inquiry alone is the weakest evidence and needs corroboration.
distractors.C: A documented procedure evidences design, not that the control actually operates.

explanation.exam_pattern: Re-performance > observation > inquiry; proving a control OPERATES is strongest by re-performing it.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Audit evidence-gathering techniques

questions.stem: While performing fieldwork, an IS auditor uncovers evidence suggesting a possible fraud by a department supervisor. What should the auditor do FIRST?

options.text: Begin a covert investigation and interrogate staff
Ignore it unless it is material to the current audit scope
Confront the supervisor and demand an explanation
Report the matter to the appropriate level of management or the audit committee, per the organization's protocol

explanation.correct: Suspected fraud should be escalated to the appropriate level of management (above those involved) or the audit committee, following the organization's protocol; the auditor does not investigate or confront alone.

distractors.A: The IS auditor is not the investigator and should not run interrogations alone.
distractors.B: Suspected fraud must be escalated regardless of the original audit scope.
distractors.C: Confronting the suspect can compromise evidence and the inquiry.

explanation.exam_pattern: Suspected fraud -> report to appropriate management/audit committee; don't investigate or confront alone.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Irregularities, illegal acts, and reporting

questions.stem: A well-developed audit finding documents the condition, the criteria, the cause, and the effect. What does the 'criteria' element represent?

options.text: The business impact or risk of the problem
The current state or problem the auditor observed
The standard, policy, or requirement that the condition is measured against
The underlying reason the problem occurred

explanation.correct: Criteria is the standard or requirement (what should be) against which the observed condition is compared.

distractors.A: That is the 'effect' (the impact or risk).
distractors.B: That is the 'condition' (what is).
distractors.D: That is the 'cause' (why it happened).

explanation.exam_pattern: Finding = Condition (what is) vs Criteria (what should be) + Cause (why) + Effect (impact).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Structure of audit findings

questions.stem: During follow-up, an IS auditor finds that a previously reported HIGH-risk weakness has not been remediated, and management has chosen to accept the risk. What is the auditor's BEST action?

options.text: Implement the fix personally to close the gap
Report that the risk remains and has been formally accepted by management, escalating to senior management/the audit committee if it exceeds risk appetite
Remove the finding because management accepted the risk

explanation.correct: An unremediated, accepted risk is still reported; if the residual risk exceeds the organization's risk appetite, the auditor escalates to senior management or the audit committee.

distractors.A: A full re-audit is disproportionate; follow-up targets the specific agreed action.
distractors.B: Remediating personally impairs independence; the fix is management's responsibility.
distractors.D: An accepted risk is documented, not deleted from the report.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unremediated high risk accepted by management -> document and escalate to governance; don't delete or fix it yourself.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 1 — Follow-up and residual risk acceptance

questions.stem: In COBIT, which activity BEST characterizes GOVERNANCE as distinct from management?

options.text: Writing the application source code for each project
Staffing and operating the service desk
Planning, building, running, and monitoring day-to-day activities
Evaluating, directing, and monitoring to set direction and oversee that objectives are met

explanation.correct: Governance (the board's role) evaluates, directs, and monitors (EDM) - setting direction and overseeing outcomes - while management plans, builds, runs, and monitors execution.

distractors.A: Writing code is a development activity, not governance.
distractors.B: Operating the service desk is an operational task.
distractors.C: Plan/Build/Run/Monitor is management's role, not governance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Governance = Evaluate/Direct/Monitor (board sets direction); management = Plan/Build/Run/Monitor (executes).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Governance vs. management of enterprise IT (COBIT)

questions.stem: Which tool helps management measure IT performance and its alignment with business objectives across multiple perspectives rather than financial measures alone?

explanation.correct: An IT balanced scorecard measures IT across several perspectives (e.g., business contribution, user, operational excellence, future orientation), linking IT performance to business goals.

distractors.A: The general ledger is a financial accounting record.
distractors.B: A firewall rule base is a technical configuration, not a performance measure.
distractors.D: Uptime alone is a single operational metric, not a multi-perspective measure of alignment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Multi-perspective measurement of IT performance/alignment = IT balanced scorecard.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — IT balanced scorecard

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of an enterprise architecture (EA)?

options.text: To provide a blueprint that aligns IT structure, data, and technology standards with business strategy

explanation.correct: An enterprise architecture is the blueprint that keeps the organization's IT structure, data, and technology standards aligned with and supporting business strategy.

distractors.A: Encryption is a control, not an architecture blueprint.
distractors.B: Help-desk staffing is an operational function.
distractors.C: Backup scheduling is an operations task, not the purpose of EA.

explanation.exam_pattern: EA = the blueprint that keeps IT standards/structure aligned with business strategy.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Enterprise architecture

questions.stem: An organization rates each IT process on a scale from 'initial/ad hoc' to 'optimized'. This is an example of using a:

explanation.correct: A capability maturity model rates process maturity on a graded scale (e.g., initial, repeatable, defined, managed, optimized), helping identify improvement priorities.

distractors.A: A penetration test probes security weaknesses, not process maturity.
distractors.C: A backup rotation scheme is an operations control.
distractors.D: A data flow diagram models how data moves through a system.

explanation.exam_pattern: Rating process maturity (initial -> optimized) = capability maturity model.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Process maturity models

questions.stem: Which type of governance document specifies a MANDATORY, uniform rule - such as requiring a specific minimum encryption algorithm on all laptops?

explanation.correct: A standard is a mandatory, specific, uniform rule (e.g., a required technology or configuration) that implements a policy.

distractors.A: A policy states high-level management intent, not a specific mandatory rule.
distractors.C: A guideline is a recommended, non-mandatory practice.
distractors.D: A procedure is the step-by-step how-to, not the mandatory rule itself.

explanation.exam_pattern: Mandatory, specific, uniform rule/technology = standard (policy=intent, procedure=steps, guideline=optional).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Standards vs. policies, procedures, guidelines

questions.stem: The IT strategic plan should be derived PRIMARILY from:

options.text: The preferences of the IT staff

explanation.correct: IT strategy must flow from and align with the business/corporate strategy so IT investments support enterprise objectives.

distractors.A: Chasing the newest technology is not the same as aligning with business goals.
distractors.B: The auditor advises on controls but does not set IT strategy.
distractors.C: Staff preference is not a strategic basis.

explanation.exam_pattern: IT strategy must flow from (align with) the business strategy.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — IT strategy alignment

questions.stem: To ensure IT investments reflect business priorities, an IT steering committee should include:

options.text: Representatives from business/user units as well as senior IT management

explanation.correct: A steering committee should be cross-functional - business/user representatives plus senior IT management - so IT delivery reflects business needs and priorities.

distractors.A: Junior developers lack the authority to set investment priorities.
distractors.B: An IT-only committee loses the business voice that prioritization requires.
distractors.D: Vendors have commercial conflicts and should not set internal priorities.

explanation.exam_pattern: Steering committee = cross-functional (business + senior IT) so IT serves business needs.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — IT steering committee composition

questions.stem: An IS auditor notes the information security policy has not been reviewed or updated in five years. What is the GREATEST concern?

options.text: The document uses an outdated font
It may no longer address current threats, technologies, and regulatory requirements

explanation.correct: Policies must be reviewed periodically; a stale policy may fail to cover current threats, technology, and regulations, leaving gaps.

distractors.A: Employees reading the policy is a good thing, not a concern.
distractors.B: Font choice is irrelevant to the control.
distractors.C: Length is not the issue; relevance is.

explanation.exam_pattern: Policies must be reviewed periodically - a stale policy may not cover current risks/regulations.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Policy lifecycle and review

questions.stem: Which combination of duties performed by ONE person represents the GREATEST segregation-of-duties concern?

options.text: Authorizing payments and reconciling the bank account that records them
Answering the help desk and writing user documentation

explanation.correct: One person who both authorizes/executes payments and reconciles the account can commit and then conceal a fraud - the classic incompatible-duties conflict.

distractors.A: Running reports is not a conflicting combination of duties.
distractors.C: Help desk and documentation are compatible, low-risk duties.
distractors.D: Attending meetings is not a duties conflict.

explanation.exam_pattern: One person who both authorizes/executes AND reconciles/records can commit and hide fraud - incompatible.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Segregation of incompatible duties

questions.stem: A data custodian (such as IT operations) is PRIMARILY responsible for:

options.text: Implementing and maintaining protection controls (backups, access enforcement) as directed by the data owner

explanation.correct: The custodian safeguards the data day to day - implementing and maintaining the controls (backup, access enforcement) that the owner specifies.

distractors.A: Classifying data is the data owner's responsibility.
distractors.B: Budget approval is a management decision, not a custodian task.
distractors.D: Risk appetite is set by senior management.

explanation.exam_pattern: Owner classifies/authorizes; custodian safeguards and maintains controls as directed.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Data owner vs. custodian

questions.stem: To avoid a conflict of interest, the information security function should ideally be organizationally independent of:

options.text: IT operations and development, whose activities it must oversee

explanation.correct: Security should not report into the IT operations/development functions it is meant to oversee, or it would be judging its own masters - a self-oversight conflict.

distractors.A: Customers are external and not part of the reporting line.
distractors.C: Marketing is unrelated to the security-oversight conflict.
distractors.D: Legal does not create the self-oversight conflict that reporting into IT ops/dev does.

explanation.exam_pattern: Security shouldn't report to the IT functions it polices (self-oversight conflict of interest).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Organizational placement of the security function

questions.stem: A policy requiring employees in sensitive positions to take at least one continuous week of vacation each year functions PRIMARILY as a control to:

options.text: Detect fraud or irregularities that require the employee's ongoing presence to conceal

explanation.correct: Mandatory vacation (like job rotation) forces an absence during which another person operates the role, surfacing fraud that needs the perpetrator present to stay hidden.

distractors.A: Mandatory vacation does not reduce payroll costs.
distractors.C: It does not speed up processing.
distractors.D: Morale may improve, but that is not the control's purpose.

explanation.exam_pattern: Mandatory vacation / job rotation surfaces fraud that needs the perpetrator present to hide it.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Mandatory vacation and job rotation

questions.stem: An organization decides NOT to launch a new online service because the associated security risk is judged too high. Which risk response is this?

explanation.correct: Choosing not to undertake the risky activity at all is risk avoidance.

distractors.A: Transfer shifts the impact to a third party (e.g., insurance).
distractors.B: Acceptance means proceeding and retaining the risk.
distractors.D: Mitigation reduces the risk with controls but still proceeds.

explanation.exam_pattern: Decline the risky activity entirely = avoidance (accept=retain, transfer=shift, mitigate=reduce).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Risk response options

questions.stem: In quantitative risk analysis, which value represents the expected annual monetary loss from a specific risk, calculated as single loss expectancy multiplied by the annualized rate of occurrence?

explanation.correct: ALE = SLE x ARO, the expected yearly monetary loss used to compare risks and justify control spending.

distractors.A: The exposure factor is the percentage of asset value lost per event, not the annual loss.
distractors.B: Risk appetite is the level of risk tolerated, not a calculated loss.
distractors.D: Residual risk is what remains after controls, not a loss figure.

explanation.exam_pattern: ALE = SLE x ARO (expected yearly loss); SLE = asset value x exposure factor.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Quantitative risk analysis (ALE/SLE/ARO)

questions.stem: Which metric is designed to give management an EARLY WARNING that risk exposure is rising toward an unacceptable level?

explanation.correct: A key risk indicator is a forward-looking metric that signals increasing risk exposure before it becomes a loss.

distractors.B: Profit margin is a financial outcome, not a risk early-warning.
distractors.C: A throughput KPI measures performance, not risk.
distractors.D: A satisfaction score measures service quality, not risk.

explanation.exam_pattern: Early-warning signal of increasing risk = key risk indicator (KRI).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Key risk indicators

questions.stem: When reliable monetary loss data is not available, which risk-analysis approach is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Waiting until a loss actually occurs
Quantitative analysis requiring precise dollar figures
Qualitative analysis using ratings such as high/medium/low

explanation.correct: When hard monetary data is lacking, qualitative analysis uses relative ratings (high/medium/low likelihood and impact) to prioritize risks.

distractors.A: Waiting for a loss is reactive, not analysis.
distractors.B: Quantitative analysis needs the monetary data that is unavailable here.
distractors.D: Skipping analysis leaves risk unmanaged.

explanation.exam_pattern: No hard dollar data -> qualitative (relative) rating; precise dollar impact -> quantitative.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Qualitative vs. quantitative risk analysis

questions.stem: How does the recovery time objective (RTO) relate to the maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) for a business process?

options.text: The RTO must always exceed the MTD
The MTD must always be zero
The RTO must be less than or equal to the MTD

explanation.correct: Recovery must complete within the maximum downtime the business can tolerate, so the RTO must be set at or below the MTD.

distractors.A: An RTO exceeding the MTD means recovery is too slow to be tolerable.
distractors.B: MTD is rarely zero; it reflects how long the process can be down.
distractors.C: They are directly related - RTO is bounded by MTD.

explanation.exam_pattern: RTO (planned recovery time) must fit within MTD (max downtime the business can bear).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — MTD, RTO, and recovery objectives

questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes a business continuity plan (BCP) from a disaster recovery plan (DRP)?

options.text: The BCP covers only IT systems
The BCP addresses keeping the whole business (people, processes, facilities) operating, while the DRP focuses on recovering IT systems and infrastructure
The DRP is broader than the BCP

explanation.correct: The BCP is the broad plan to keep the business functioning; the DRP is the IT-focused subset that restores systems and infrastructure.

distractors.A: The BCP spans people, processes, and facilities, not IT alone.
distractors.C: They are related but not identical.
distractors.D: The BCP is the broader of the two, not the DRP.

explanation.exam_pattern: BCP = keep the business running (broad); DRP = restore IT (a subset of BCP).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — Business continuity vs. disaster recovery

questions.stem: An IS auditor reviewing business continuity would be MOST concerned to find that the BCP:

options.text: Is stored in a shared document library
Has never been tested or updated since it was first written

explanation.correct: An untested, outdated BCP may fail when invoked; continuity plans must be tested and maintained to stay effective.

distractors.A: A current org chart is a sign the plan is maintained - good, not a concern.
distractors.B: A shared library is reasonable storage (ideally with an accessible offsite copy).
distractors.D: Contact lists are expected, useful plan content.

explanation.exam_pattern: An untested, outdated BCP may fail when needed - test and maintain it.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 2 — BCP testing and maintenance

questions.stem: Using PERT with an optimistic estimate (O), most likely estimate (M), and pessimistic estimate (P), the expected activity duration is calculated as:

options.text: The largest of O, M, and P

explanation.correct: PERT weights the most likely estimate four times: expected time = (O + 4M + P) / 6.

distractors.A: The midpoint of O and P ignores M entirely.
distractors.B: A simple average ignores the extra weight on the most likely estimate.
distractors.C: Taking the maximum is overly pessimistic and not the PERT formula.

explanation.exam_pattern: PERT expected time = (O + 4M + P) / 6 (the most likely estimate is weighted x4).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — PERT estimation

questions.stem: Which project tool shows tasks as horizontal bars along a timeline and is used mainly to track progress against the schedule?

explanation.correct: A Gantt chart plots tasks as bars on a timeline, making it easy to track schedule and progress (though it does not highlight the critical path the way a network diagram does).

distractors.B: A data flow diagram models how data moves through a system.
distractors.C: An entity-relationship diagram models data relationships.
distractors.D: A decision table maps conditions to actions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Bars on a timeline for scheduling/progress = Gantt chart.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Project scheduling tools (Gantt)

questions.stem: A task that lies ON the critical path is delayed by three days. Assuming no corrective action, what is the effect?

options.text: There is no effect because the task has slack
The entire project's completion is delayed by three days

explanation.correct: Critical-path tasks have zero float, so any delay to them pushes out the whole project's completion by the same amount.

distractors.A: Critical-path tasks have zero slack/float by definition.
distractors.C: A delay cannot make the project finish earlier.
distractors.D: A critical-path delay affects the overall project end date, not just non-critical tasks.

explanation.exam_pattern: Critical-path tasks have zero float - any delay to them delays the whole project.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Critical path and float

questions.stem: Which technique measures whether a project is on schedule and within budget by comparing the planned value, earned value, and actual cost of work?

explanation.correct: Earned value management integrates scope, schedule, and cost by comparing planned value, earned value, and actual cost to show schedule and cost performance.

distractors.A: A feasibility study assesses viability up front, not ongoing performance.
distractors.C: A structured walkthrough is a review technique, not a performance measure.
distractors.D: Function point analysis sizes software; it does not track schedule/cost performance.

explanation.exam_pattern: Integrated schedule+cost performance (planned vs earned vs actual) = earned value management.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Earned value management

questions.stem: When user requirements are unclear or evolving, which development approach builds successive working models for users to react to and refine?

explanation.correct: Prototyping iteratively builds working models that users evaluate, clarifying unclear or evolving requirements before full build.

distractors.B: Big-bang integration is a testing/integration approach, not a requirements technique.
distractors.C: Direct cutover is a system conversion strategy.
distractors.D: Waterfall fixes requirements up front and suits well-understood needs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unclear/evolving requirements -> iterative prototyping to refine with users.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — SDLC approaches (prototyping)

questions.stem: When auditing a project using agile/rapid development, what is the IS auditor's PRIMARY concern?

options.text: That the team holds daily stand-up meetings
That software is delivered in increments
That speed and reduced formality may weaken documentation, controls, and audit trails

explanation.correct: Agile/RAD's speed and lighter ceremony can erode documentation, controls, and traceability; the auditor verifies that adequate controls and audit trails still exist.

distractors.A: Frequent user involvement is a strength of agile.
distractors.B: Daily stand-ups are a normal, beneficial agile practice.
distractors.C: Incremental delivery is a feature of agile, not a concern.

explanation.exam_pattern: Agile/RAD's risk to the auditor = lighter documentation/controls - confirm controls and traceability remain.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Agile/RAD and control considerations

questions.stem: An organization licenses critical software from a small vendor and worries the vendor could go out of business. Which arrangement BEST protects its ability to maintain the software?

options.text: A source code escrow agreement with a trusted third party

explanation.correct: A source code escrow holds the source with a neutral third party, released to the licensee on defined triggers (e.g., vendor bankruptcy) so the software can be maintained.

distractors.B: Payment terms do not secure access to the source code.
distractors.C: Marketing budget is irrelevant to this risk.
distractors.D: Bandwidth has nothing to do with vendor failure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Vendor-failure protection for licensed software = source code escrow (released on defined triggers).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Software acquisition and source code escrow

questions.stem: Which type of testing examines the internal logic and code paths of a program, requiring knowledge of its internal structure?

explanation.correct: White-box testing inspects internal logic and code paths, so it requires knowledge of the program's internal structure.

distractors.B: Parallel testing is a system conversion method, not a code-logic test.
distractors.C: Black-box testing checks functionality without knowledge of internal code.
distractors.D: User acceptance testing validates business requirements from the user's perspective.

explanation.exam_pattern: Internal logic/code = white-box; external behavior without internals = black-box.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Testing methods (white-box vs. black-box)

questions.stem: Which conversion strategy introduces the new system gradually, module by module or location by location, over time?

explanation.correct: A phased changeover rolls the new system out incrementally (by module or site), lowering risk per step but taking longer and requiring old/new interfaces during transition.

distractors.A: Direct/big-bang switches everything at once.
distractors.B: 'No changeover' is not a strategy.
distractors.C: Parallel runs the old and new systems together for comparison.

explanation.exam_pattern: Gradual, incremental rollout = phased changeover (lower risk than big-bang, but longer).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Changeover strategies (phased)

questions.stem: An organization deploys a new system to one branch office first to validate it before rolling it out company-wide. This conversion approach is:

options.text: Direct changeover across all sites at once

explanation.correct: A pilot changeover proves the system at one site/group first, containing risk before an organization-wide rollout.

distractors.B: Direct changeover deploys everywhere at once with no trial site.
distractors.C: Big-bang conversion switches the whole organization simultaneously.
distractors.D: Parallel runs the old and new systems together, not a single trial site.

explanation.exam_pattern: Try it at one site/group first, then expand = pilot conversion.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Changeover strategies (pilot)

questions.stem: Before migrating data from a legacy system, the project cleans up duplicate, incomplete, and inconsistent records. What is the PRIMARY purpose of this data-cleansing step?

options.text: To encrypt the data in transit
To prevent carrying poor-quality 'garbage' data into the new system
To speed up the office network

explanation.correct: Cleansing corrects duplicates and errors in legacy data so poor-quality data is not migrated into the new system (garbage in, garbage out).

distractors.A: Encryption is a confidentiality control, not the goal of cleansing.
distractors.C: User training is a separate implementation activity.
distractors.D: Network speed is unrelated to data cleansing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Clean legacy data before migration so errors/duplicates aren't carried forward.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Data migration and cleansing

questions.stem: A post-implementation review should compare the system's actual results PRIMARILY against:

options.text: The costs, benefits, and objectives projected in the original business case
The preferences of the development team

explanation.correct: A PIR measures the live system's actual costs, benefits, and performance against the original business case that justified the project.

distractors.B: Team preference is not the approved baseline.
distractors.C: Marketing claims are not an objective benchmark.
distractors.D: Industry trends are not the project's success criteria.

explanation.exam_pattern: PIR measures actual outcomes against the original business case (planned costs/benefits/objectives).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Post-implementation review and benefits

questions.stem: When an IS auditor participates in a post-implementation review, the auditor is PRIMARILY concerned with whether:

options.text: The launch event was well attended
The system uses the latest framework
Adequate controls were built into the delivered system and the system met its objectives

explanation.correct: The IS auditor's PIR focus is whether adequate controls are present and operating and whether the system achieved its intended objectives and benefits.

distractors.A: Event attendance is irrelevant to control adequacy.
distractors.B: Using the latest framework is not the audit concern.
distractors.D: Team satisfaction does not evidence controls or benefits.

explanation.exam_pattern: In a PIR, the auditor focuses on control adequacy and whether objectives/benefits were achieved.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 3 — Auditor's role in post-implementation review

questions.stem: Which control BEST ensures that only authorized, tested program changes are moved into production?

options.text: Changes are approved through change management and migrated by someone other than the developer who wrote them
Changes are applied directly to production and documented only if problems arise
Developers move their own changes whenever convenient
No approval is required for small changes

explanation.correct: Authorized and tested changes migrated by someone other than the developer enforces both change control and segregation of duties between development and production.

distractors.B: Applying changes directly and documenting only on failure is uncontrolled.
distractors.C: Developers promoting their own code breaks segregation of duties.
distractors.D: 'No approval for small changes' is a loophole that undermines change control.

explanation.exam_pattern: Authorized + tested + segregated migration (developer doesn't promote own code) = sound change control.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Change and release management controls

questions.stem: What is the GREATEST risk of applying vendor security patches directly to production systems without testing them first?

options.text: The systems will become more secure
A patch could introduce incompatibilities that disrupt or crash production services

explanation.correct: An untested patch may be incompatible and destabilize or crash production; patches should be tested in a non-production environment first.

distractors.A: Vendors do not revoke support simply for applying patches.
distractors.B: Install speed is not a meaningful risk.
distractors.C: Added security is the goal, not a risk.

explanation.exam_pattern: Patch untested in production -> risk of outages/instability; test patches before deployment.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Patch management

questions.stem: An IS auditor wants assurance that scheduled batch jobs complete successfully and that failures are handled. The BEST evidence is:

options.text: A verbal assurance from an operator
The brand of the job-scheduling software
The color of the operations console screen
Review of the job schedule and exception/error logs showing failures are detected and reruns are performed

explanation.correct: Reviewing the job schedule and exception logs provides objective evidence that failed jobs are detected, escalated, and rerun.

distractors.A: A verbal assurance is weak, uncorroborated evidence.
distractors.B: The software brand says nothing about whether jobs complete.
distractors.C: Screen color is irrelevant.

explanation.exam_pattern: Batch assurance = review the schedule and exception logs for detection and rerun of failed jobs.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Job scheduling and batch monitoring

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a configuration management database (CMDB)?

options.text: To maintain accurate records of IT assets (configuration items) and their relationships to support change and incident management

explanation.correct: A CMDB is the authoritative inventory of configuration items and their relationships, supporting change, incident, and problem management.

distractors.B: Traffic filtering is a firewall role.
distractors.C: Passwords belong in an identity/credential store, not the CMDB.
distractors.D: Data backup is a separate function.

explanation.exam_pattern: CMDB = authoritative inventory of configuration items and their relationships.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Configuration management

questions.stem: An IS auditor finds that a critical financial report is produced by a complex end-user spreadsheet maintained by one analyst. What is the GREATEST concern?

options.text: The analyst sometimes works from home
The spreadsheet lacks the change control, testing, and validation applied to formal applications, risking undetected errors
The file has a long name

explanation.correct: User-developed spreadsheets driving key decisions typically lack formal change control, testing, and validation, so errors can go undetected - a data-integrity risk.

distractors.A: Formatting is not a control weakness.
distractors.B: Remote work is not the core concern.
distractors.D: The file name is irrelevant.

explanation.exam_pattern: End-user spreadsheets driving key decisions lack formal controls (change/test/validation) - a data-integrity risk.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — End-user computing controls

questions.stem: In an electronic data interchange (EDI) environment, which control BEST provides assurance that inbound trading-partner transactions are complete and were not lost?

options.text: Transmitting functional acknowledgments and reconciling control totals for each batch received
Storing messages in a larger database

explanation.correct: Functional acknowledgments confirm receipt, and reconciling control totals confirms that every transaction in a batch was received and processed - completeness.

distractors.B: Printing messages does not reconcile what was sent versus received.
distractors.C: Database size is irrelevant to transaction completeness.
distractors.D: UI appearance does not assure completeness.

explanation.exam_pattern: EDI completeness = functional acknowledgments + control-total reconciliation at receipt.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — EDI controls

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The input control that detects transposition and transcription errors in a key field (such as an account number) by appending a calculated extra digit is called a check ______.

explanation.correct: A check digit is a digit computed from the other digits of a key field; if the field is mis-keyed or transposed, the recomputed check digit will not match, flagging the error.
explanation.exam_pattern: Catch mis-keyed/transposed digits in an identifier = check digit.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Input/edit controls (check digit)

questions.stem: A batch process sums the account-number field of all records (a total with no intrinsic meaning) and compares it before and after transfer. This control is a:

explanation.correct: A hash total is a meaningless control sum of a field (e.g., account numbers) used only to verify that the batch is complete and unchanged between sender and receiver.

distractors.A: A check digit validates a single field's keystrokes, not batch completeness.
distractors.C: A parity bit detects single-bit transmission errors, not batch totals.
distractors.D: A digital signature provides authentication/non-repudiation, not batch completeness.

explanation.exam_pattern: A meaningless control sum over a field to prove batch completeness = hash total.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Batch/processing controls (hash totals)

questions.stem: An application rejects any entry for 'hours worked in a week' that is greater than 168. Which type of input validation is this?

explanation.correct: A range (limit) check verifies that a value falls within predefined bounds - here, that weekly hours cannot exceed 168.

distractors.A: A hash total verifies batch completeness, not a single value's range.
distractors.C: A check digit validates an identifier's keystrokes, not a value's reasonableness.
distractors.D: Referential integrity enforces key relationships in a database.

explanation.exam_pattern: Value must fall within predefined bounds = range/limit check.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Input validation (range/limit checks)

questions.stem: An organization performs a weekly full backup and daily incremental backups. To fully restore after a Thursday failure, what must be applied?

options.text: The last full backup plus every incremental taken since, applied in order
The last full plus the single most recent incremental

explanation.correct: Incremental backups each capture changes since the previous backup, so a full restore needs the last full plus all subsequent incrementals applied in sequence.

distractors.A: A single incremental misses the earlier days' changes.
distractors.C: 'Full + one incremental' describes a differential scheme, not incremental.
distractors.D: The full alone misses all the daily changes since.

explanation.exam_pattern: Incremental restore = last FULL + ALL incrementals in order (fast backup, slower/complex restore).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Backup types and restoration

questions.stem: Which statement about the archive bit is correct?

options.text: Only a differential backup clears it
Neither incremental nor differential backups touch it
Both incremental and differential backups clear it
An incremental backup clears (resets) the archive bit, whereas a differential backup leaves it set

explanation.correct: Incremental backups clear the archive bit (so the next incremental only grabs new changes), while differentials leave it set - which is why differentials keep growing until the next full backup.

distractors.A: It is the incremental, not the differential, that clears the bit.
distractors.B: Both types read the archive bit, and incremental resets it.
distractors.C: A differential does not clear the archive bit.

explanation.exam_pattern: Incremental CLEARS the archive bit; differential does NOT - so differentials accumulate changes since the last full.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Backup mechanics (archive bit)

questions.stem: An administrator argues that RAID 5 on the server makes backups unnecessary. Why should the IS auditor disagree?

options.text: RAID eliminates the need for a UPS
RAID protects against disk hardware failure but not against data corruption, accidental deletion, ransomware, or site disaster

explanation.correct: RAID provides disk fault tolerance/availability, but it faithfully replicates corruption, deletions, and ransomware, and offers no protection against site disaster - so it is not a substitute for backups.

distractors.A: RAID does not encrypt data.
distractors.B: RAID is unrelated to power protection.
distractors.C: RAID does not provide offsite copies.

explanation.exam_pattern: RAID = disk fault tolerance/availability, NOT a backup (no protection from deletion/corruption/disaster).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — RAID vs. backup

questions.stem: Which technique transmits database transaction logs to an offsite location in near real time to minimize data loss (a very small RPO)?

options.text: Monthly tape rotation to a local cabinet

explanation.correct: Remote journaling streams transaction LOGS offsite in near real time, so very little data is lost if the primary site fails - a small RPO. (It differs from electronic vaulting, which transfers bulk backup data in periodic batches, and from database shadowing, which keeps a real-time duplicate.)

distractors.B: Printing reports is not a data-recovery mechanism.
distractors.C: Monthly local tapes leave a large data-loss window and sit at the primary location.
distractors.D: An annual backup leaves an enormous RPO.

explanation.exam_pattern: Near-real-time offsite transaction logs = remote journaling -> small RPO (electronic vaulting = periodic batch transfer; database shadowing = real-time duplicate).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Electronic vaulting and remote journaling

questions.stem: Why should backup copies be stored at an offsite location that is geographically separated from the primary site?

options.text: So that a single local disaster (fire, flood) cannot destroy both the primary data and its backups
To reduce the organization's electricity costs
So that the tapes accumulate more mileage

explanation.correct: Geographic separation ensures one local disaster cannot wipe out both production data and its backups at the same time.

distractors.B: Offsite storage is about disaster resilience, not electricity cost.
distractors.C: Slower restores are a drawback, not the purpose.
distractors.D: Tape mileage is not a reason for offsite storage.

explanation.exam_pattern: Separate offsite storage so one disaster can't take out both production and backups.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Offsite backup storage

questions.stem: A recovery site that has hardware and network connectivity in place but requires recent data and final configuration to be loaded before operations resume is a:

explanation.correct: A warm site has hardware and connectivity ready but needs current data and final setup, giving a moderate recovery time at moderate cost - between hot and cold.

distractors.B: A reciprocal site is a mutual-aid arrangement with another organization, not a staged facility.
distractors.C: A hot site is fully equipped and current, ready within hours with no major load step.
distractors.D: A cold site provides only space, power, and HVAC - no installed hardware.

explanation.exam_pattern: Partial equipment, needs data/config load, moderate time/cost = warm site.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Recovery site types (warm)

questions.stem: Which alternate-processing option is a transportable, pre-configured unit (e.g., a trailer) that can be moved to a location and connected to restore operations?

explanation.correct: A mobile site is a transportable, pre-equipped unit brought to a location and connected to resume operations - useful when a fixed alternate facility is impractical.

distractors.B: A hot site is a fixed, fully equipped facility.
distractors.C: A cold site is a fixed, empty conditioned facility.
distractors.D: A reciprocal agreement uses a partner's existing data center.

explanation.exam_pattern: Transportable, pre-equipped unit brought to a site = mobile site.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Recovery site types (mobile)

questions.stem: Which disaster recovery test is the LEAST disruptive and typically performed FIRST to validate the plan on paper?

options.text: An unannounced shutdown of the production data center

explanation.correct: A checklist/structured walkthrough reviews the plan on paper with no live processing, making it the least disruptive and a natural first step before more realistic tests.

distractors.A: An unannounced production shutdown is the most disruptive and risky option.
distractors.C: A full-interruption test shifts live processing to the alternate site - the most disruptive.
distractors.D: A parallel test processes real workloads at the alternate site - more disruptive than a walkthrough.

explanation.exam_pattern: Start DR testing with a low-risk checklist/walkthrough; progress toward parallel then full-interruption.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — DR test types and progression

questions.stem: During disaster recovery, in what order should systems and processes be restored?

options.text: In order of business criticality, with the most time-sensitive processes (per the BIA) restored first
Starting with the least important systems
In alphabetical order of system name
In the order the systems were originally purchased

explanation.correct: Recovery is prioritized by business criticality from the BIA, restoring the most time-sensitive processes first to limit business impact.

distractors.B: Restoring least-important systems first wastes the critical recovery window.
distractors.C: Alphabetical order ignores business priority.
distractors.D: Purchase order has no bearing on business criticality.

explanation.exam_pattern: Recover the most business-critical/time-sensitive systems first, driven by the BIA.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Recovery prioritization

questions.stem: An IS auditor finds that the only copies of the disaster recovery plan are stored in the primary data center. Why is this a concern?

options.text: The plan would take up too much shelf space
Staff would become too familiar with the plan
A disaster that destroys the data center would also destroy the plan needed to recover
The plan would be read too often

explanation.correct: If the DRP exists only at the primary site, the same disaster that takes out the site destroys the plan; current copies must be kept offsite and accessible to recovery teams.

distractors.A: Shelf space is irrelevant.
distractors.B: Familiarity with the plan is desirable.
distractors.D: Frequent reading of the plan is beneficial, not a risk.

explanation.exam_pattern: Keep accessible DRP copies offsite - a plan trapped in the destroyed site is useless.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — DRP availability and storage

questions.stem: In IT service management, how is the PRIORITY of an incident normally determined?

options.text: By combining its impact and its urgency
By how long the assigned technician has worked there
By the alphabetical name of the affected system

explanation.correct: Incident priority is derived by combining impact (how much/how many are affected) with urgency (how quickly resolution is needed).

distractors.B: Technician tenure is irrelevant to incident priority.
distractors.C: The reporter's identity alone does not set priority.
distractors.D: The system's name does not determine priority.

explanation.exam_pattern: Incident priority = impact (how much/many) x urgency (how fast it's needed).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Incident prioritization

questions.stem: In problem management, a problem whose root cause has been identified and for which a workaround exists is recorded as a:

explanation.correct: Once root cause and a workaround are documented, a problem is logged as a known error, speeding resolution of future related incidents.

distractors.A: A major incident is a high-impact incident, not a documented root cause plus workaround.
distractors.B: A service request is a routine user request (e.g., access or equipment).
distractors.D: A change request proposes a modification to the environment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Root cause found + workaround documented = known error.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Problem management (known error)

questions.stem: In ITIL-based operations, the service desk functions PRIMARILY as:

options.text: The team that writes application code
The group that approves the IT budget
The single point of contact (SPOC) between users and IT for incidents and service requests

explanation.correct: The service desk is the single point of contact for users - logging, routing, and tracking incidents and service requests.

distractors.A: Coding is a development activity, not the service desk's role.
distractors.B: Budget approval is a management responsibility.
distractors.C: External audit is independent of the service desk.

explanation.exam_pattern: Service desk = single point of contact for users (logs/routes incidents and requests).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Service desk function

questions.stem: An incident requires a decision to authorize significant emergency spending to resolve it. Which type of escalation is appropriate?

options.text: Functional escalation to a technical specialist team
Logging it as a known error
Hierarchical escalation up the management chain

explanation.correct: Decisions needing authority (like approving emergency spend) require hierarchical escalation up the management chain.

distractors.A: Closing the incident leaves it unresolved.
distractors.B: Functional escalation obtains technical expertise, not spending authority.
distractors.C: A known error is a problem-management record, not an escalation for authority.

explanation.exam_pattern: Need authority/management decision = hierarchical escalation; need expertise = functional escalation.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Incident escalation

questions.stem: Which property of a database transaction guarantees that it either completes entirely or has no effect at all (no partial updates)?

explanation.correct: Atomicity is the all-or-nothing property: a transaction either fully commits or is completely rolled back, leaving no partial updates.

distractors.A: Isolation keeps concurrent transactions from interfering with each other.
distractors.B: Consistency keeps the database in a valid state that satisfies all constraints.
distractors.D: Durability ensures committed results survive a subsequent failure.

explanation.exam_pattern: All-or-nothing transaction = Atomicity (the 'A' in ACID).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Transaction integrity (ACID)

questions.stem: Which database control prevents two concurrent transactions from overwriting each other's updates (the 'lost update' problem)?

explanation.correct: Locking/concurrency control serializes conflicting access so simultaneous transactions cannot overwrite one another (a deadlock is two transactions each waiting on the other's lock).

distractors.A: A check digit validates input keystrokes, not concurrency.
distractors.C: Normalization reduces redundancy in the schema design, not runtime concurrency.
distractors.D: Encryption protects confidentiality, not concurrent-update integrity.

explanation.exam_pattern: Serialize concurrent updates to prevent lost updates = locking/concurrency control.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Database concurrency control

questions.stem: A database administrator gives a group of users a view that exposes only certain columns and rows of a table. This BEST supports which objective?

options.text: Enforcing least-privilege logical access to data

explanation.correct: A view restricts users to only the rows/columns they need, implementing least-privilege access at the data level.

distractors.A: A view does not affect disk performance.
distractors.C: A view is not a backup mechanism.
distractors.D: A view is not encryption.

explanation.exam_pattern: Restrict users to specific columns/rows with a database view = least-privilege data access.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Database access controls (views)

questions.stem: After a database server crash, which mechanism allows the DBMS to restore the database to a consistent state by undoing incomplete transactions and reapplying committed ones?

options.text: Transaction logs/journals with rollback and roll-forward

explanation.correct: The DBMS uses transaction logs/journals (with checkpoints) to roll back uncommitted transactions and roll forward committed ones, restoring a consistent state after a crash.

distractors.B: The data dictionary defines metadata, not recovery state.
distractors.C: A hash total is a batch-completeness control.
distractors.D: Referential integrity enforces key relationships, not crash recovery.

explanation.exam_pattern: Crash recovery to a consistent state = transaction logs + rollback (undo) / roll-forward (reapply).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Database recovery (logging, checkpoints)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: The repository that defines each data element, its format, attributes, and relationships (the database's metadata) is the data ______.

explanation.correct: The data dictionary holds metadata - the definitions, formats, attributes, and relationships of the data elements - supporting consistency and controlled change.
explanation.exam_pattern: Metadata repository defining data elements/attributes/relationships = data dictionary.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 4 — Data dictionary

questions.stem: Which access control model enforces access decisions using system-assigned security labels and clearances that users cannot change, making it suitable for high-security environments?

explanation.correct: MAC uses system-enforced labels and clearances that users cannot override, the most restrictive model, favored in military/high-security settings.

distractors.A: RBAC assigns access by job role, not by security labels/clearances.
distractors.C: 'No access control' is not a model.
distractors.D: DAC lets the data owner grant access at their discretion - less restrictive.

explanation.exam_pattern: Labels/clearances, system-enforced, most restrictive = MAC; owner-granted = DAC; role-based = RBAC.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Access control models (MAC)

questions.stem: A large organization with frequent staff moves wants to simplify access administration and enforce least privilege consistently. Which access control model is MOST suitable?

options.text: Assigning permissions individually to each user
Discretionary access managed ad hoc by each user

explanation.correct: RBAC assigns permissions to roles and users to roles, so access changes with the job - scaling cleanly and enforcing least privilege despite frequent moves.

distractors.B: Per-user permissions do not scale and drift out of alignment over time.
distractors.C: Ad hoc discretionary access is inconsistent and hard to govern.
distractors.D: Universal administrator rights violate least privilege entirely.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scale + consistency + least privilege across many users = RBAC (permissions by role).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Role-based access control

questions.stem: When comparing biometric systems, which single metric BEST indicates overall accuracy, measured where the false acceptance rate equals the false rejection rate?

options.text: The crossover error rate (CER/EER), where lower is better

explanation.correct: The crossover error rate (equal error rate) is the point where FAR equals FRR; a lower CER indicates a more accurate biometric system and allows fair comparison.

distractors.A: FAR alone (Type II error - accepting an impostor) describes only one error type at one threshold.
distractors.B: Enrollment time is a usability factor, not accuracy.
distractors.C: FRR alone (Type I error - rejecting a legitimate user) also describes only one error type.

explanation.exam_pattern: Compare biometrics by the CER/EER (FAR=FRR) - lower CER = more accurate. (FRR=Type I, FAR=Type II.)

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Biometric accuracy (FAR/FRR/CER)

questions.stem: Which control is MOST important to prevent access misuse when an employee is involuntarily terminated?

options.text: Promptly disabling the employee's access, coordinated with the termination

explanation.correct: Access should be revoked immediately, ideally at or before the moment of an involuntary termination, to prevent retaliatory misuse.

distractors.A: Archiving emails does not disable the account.
distractors.C: An email announcement does not remove the person's access.
distractors.D: A quarterly review is far too slow to address an immediate termination.

explanation.exam_pattern: On termination (especially involuntary), revoke/disable access immediately - don't wait for the periodic review.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Access deprovisioning / termination

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY security risk introduced by single sign-on (SSO)?

options.text: Users must remember many more passwords
Each application requires a separate login
A compromised set of SSO credentials can grant an attacker access to all connected systems

explanation.correct: SSO concentrates risk: one compromised credential can unlock every connected system, so it should be protected with strong (multi-factor) authentication.

distractors.A: SSO reduces the number of passwords users must remember.
distractors.B: SSO removes the need for separate logins - that is its purpose.
distractors.D: SSO generally speeds access rather than slowing it.

explanation.exam_pattern: SSO convenience concentrates risk - one compromised credential unlocks everything (protect it with MFA).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Single sign-on

questions.stem: Where should an organization place its public-facing web and email servers to keep them separated from the internal corporate network?

options.text: Outside any firewall on the public internet
In a DMZ (screened subnet) between external and internal firewalls

explanation.correct: A DMZ/screened subnet isolates internet-facing servers between two firewalls, so a compromise of a public server does not directly expose the internal network.

distractors.A: No-firewall exposure leaves the servers and network unprotected.
distractors.B: Placing public servers on the internal LAN exposes internal systems if they are breached.
distractors.D: Workstations are inappropriate hosts for public services.

explanation.exam_pattern: Internet-facing servers belong in a DMZ/screened subnet, isolated from the internal network.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Network segmentation (DMZ)

questions.stem: Which type of firewall inspects traffic at the application layer, can hide internal addresses, and makes connections on behalf of clients?

explanation.correct: An application-level gateway (proxy) inspects traffic at the application layer, proxies connections for clients, and hides internal addresses - deeper control than packet filtering.

distractors.A: A static packet filter only checks header fields at lower layers.
distractors.C: A media converter changes the physical medium and performs no filtering.
distractors.D: A hub is a passive repeater with no filtering.

explanation.exam_pattern: Deep application-layer inspection + proxies connections + hides internal hosts = application-level gateway (proxy).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Firewall types (application gateway)

questions.stem: Which network design BEST limits an attacker's ability to move laterally and reach all internal systems after compromising one host?

options.text: Segmenting the network into zones/VLANs with filtering between them
Using a single flat network for simplicity
Giving every device a public IP address

explanation.correct: Segmenting the network into zones/VLANs with filtering between them contains a breach and restricts lateral movement from a compromised host.

distractors.A: Disabling logging hides attacker activity and aids, not limits, the attacker.
distractors.C: A flat network lets an intruder reach everything once inside.
distractors.D: Public IPs on every device widen the attack surface.

explanation.exam_pattern: Segment the network (zones/VLANs) to contain breaches and limit lateral movement.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Network segmentation

questions.stem: An IS auditor finds a wireless LAN still secured with WEP. What is the PRIMARY concern?

options.text: WEP is incompatible with modern laptops
WEP is cryptographically weak and easily broken; it should be replaced with WPA2/WPA3
WEP uses too much electrical power

explanation.correct: WEP's encryption is fundamentally broken and can be cracked quickly, so wireless should use WPA2/WPA3 (AES) instead.

distractors.A: The concern is weak security, not speed.
distractors.B: Compatibility is not the primary concern - weak encryption is.
distractors.D: Power consumption is not the issue.

explanation.exam_pattern: WEP is broken - require WPA2/WPA3 (AES) for wireless.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Wireless security

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: A decoy system deliberately exposed to attract attackers so their activity can be detected and studied is called a ______.

explanation.correct: A honeypot is a decoy with no production purpose; any interaction with it is suspicious, so it helps detect, divert, and study attackers.
explanation.exam_pattern: Decoy to lure/detect/study attackers = honeypot.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Deception technologies (honeypot)

questions.stem: What should PRIMARILY determine how long an organization retains a category of records?

options.text: The preference of the newest employee
The amount of free disk space available

explanation.correct: Retention periods are driven by legal, regulatory, and business requirements; keeping data longer than required raises cost and risk, while deleting too early can breach obligations.

distractors.B: How 'interesting' data is has no bearing on required retention.
distractors.C: Individual preference is not a governance driver.
distractors.D: Free disk space is not a valid basis for retention decisions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Retention periods come from legal/regulatory/business requirements - not convenience.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Data retention

questions.stem: Which method BEST ensures that highly sensitive data on decommissioned hard drives cannot be recovered?

options.text: Deleting the files and emptying the recycle bin
Physical destruction, degaussing, or cryptographic erasure of the media
Performing a quick format of the drive

explanation.correct: Physical destruction, degaussing, or cryptographic erase defeats data remanence so sensitive data cannot be reconstructed from retired media.

distractors.A: Renaming files changes nothing about recoverability.
distractors.B: Deleting files and emptying the recycle bin leaves the data recoverable.
distractors.D: A quick format does not overwrite the underlying data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Defeat data remanence with degaussing, crypto-erase, or physical destruction - not simple delete/format.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Media sanitization and data remanence

questions.stem: After data has been classified, what is the NEXT step to ensure it is protected consistently throughout its life cycle?

options.text: Label the data and apply handling procedures (storage, transmission, disposal) appropriate to its classification
Publish all of it to the intranet
Delete the classification so it is simpler

explanation.correct: Classification is only useful if data is then labeled and handled - stored, transmitted, and disposed of - according to procedures matching its sensitivity level.

distractors.B: Publishing broadly ignores the classification.
distractors.C: Discarding the classification defeats the scheme.
distractors.D: Encrypting only public data misdirects protection away from sensitive data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Classification is only useful if data is then labeled and handled per its level.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Data labeling and handling

questions.stem: Which technology inspects content to detect and block unauthorized transmission of sensitive data via email, web uploads, or removable media?

explanation.correct: Data loss prevention inspects content against classification/policy and blocks or alerts on unauthorized exfiltration through channels such as email, web, and USB.
