distractors.B: A UPS supplies backup power.
distractors.C: A hypervisor runs virtual machines.
distractors.D: A load balancer distributes traffic across servers.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect/block sensitive-data exfiltration by content = data loss prevention (DLP).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Data loss prevention

questions.stem: To send a confidential message so that ONLY the intended recipient can read it, the sender should encrypt it with:

explanation.correct: Encrypting with the recipient's public key means only the recipient's matching private key can decrypt it, providing confidentiality to that recipient.

distractors.A: Encrypting with the sender's private key creates a signature anyone can read with the public key - not confidentiality.
distractors.B: The sender's public key cannot be decrypted by the recipient alone.
distractors.C: A hash is one-way and cannot be decrypted, so it provides no confidentiality.

explanation.exam_pattern: Confidentiality to a recipient = encrypt with the RECIPIENT's PUBLIC key (only their private key decrypts).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Asymmetric encryption for confidentiality

questions.stem: Which technique BEST allows a recipient to verify that a downloaded file has not been altered in transit?

options.text: Opening the file to see if it looks right
Comparing a cryptographic hash (message digest) of the file against the published value

explanation.correct: A cryptographic hash is a one-way digest; if the recomputed hash matches the published value, the file is unchanged - this verifies integrity.

distractors.A: A visual check does not detect subtle tampering.
distractors.C: Renaming proves nothing about integrity.
distractors.D: File size is a weak indicator that an attacker can easily preserve.

explanation.exam_pattern: Detect tampering by comparing cryptographic hashes (integrity) - a hash is one-way, no key.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Hashing and integrity

questions.stem: Which mechanism provides REAL-TIME checking of whether a digital certificate has been revoked?

options.text: A certificate revocation list (CRL) published periodically
The length of the public key

explanation.correct: OCSP queries the certificate's status in real time, returning good/revoked/unknown, unlike a periodically published list.

distractors.A: A CRL is published on a schedule, so it can be stale between updates.
distractors.C: The expiry date reflects validity period, not revocation.
distractors.D: Key length is unrelated to revocation status.

explanation.exam_pattern: Real-time revocation check = OCSP; periodically published list = CRL.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Certificate revocation (OCSP/CRL)

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY challenge of using symmetric encryption among many parties?

options.text: It requires a certificate authority for every message
Securely distributing and managing the shared secret keys, whose number grows rapidly with participants
It is far too slow to use in practice

explanation.correct: Symmetric encryption is fast, but its weakness is secure key distribution/management - the number of keys grows roughly as n(n-1)/2 as participants increase.

distractors.A: Symmetric encryption handles large data well.
distractors.B: It does not need a CA for every message.
distractors.D: Symmetric algorithms are fast, not too slow.

explanation.exam_pattern: Symmetric is fast but its weakness is secure key distribution/management (key count = n(n-1)/2).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Symmetric key management

questions.stem: Which TWO security services does a digital signature provide? (Choose two.)

options.text: Integrity (detecting if the message was altered)
High availability of the mail server
Confidentiality (hiding the message contents from eavesdroppers)

explanation.correct: A digital signature (the message digest encrypted with the sender's private key) provides integrity and non-repudiation (along with sender authentication).

distractors.C: Availability is unrelated to digital signatures.
distractors.D: A signature does not hide the message; confidentiality requires separately encrypting with the recipient's public key.

explanation.exam_pattern: Digital signature = integrity + authentication + non-repudiation, NOT confidentiality.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Digital signature services

questions.stem: Why is synchronized time (e.g., via NTP) across servers and network devices IMPORTANT for security monitoring and investigations?

options.text: It lets log events from different systems be accurately correlated and sequenced during analysis and forensics
It reduces the organization's electricity use

explanation.correct: Without synchronized clocks, events from different systems cannot be reliably correlated or placed in sequence, which undermines SIEM correlation and forensic reconstruction.

distractors.B: Time sync does not affect power use.
distractors.C: NTP does not encrypt logs.
distractors.D: It does not speed up backups.

explanation.exam_pattern: Without synchronized clocks you can't reliably correlate/sequence logs across systems (SIEM/forensics depend on it).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Log correlation and time synchronization

questions.stem: Which intrusion detection method is MOST likely to detect a previously unknown (zero-day) attack?

options.text: A static list of blocked IP addresses
Signature-based detection matching known attack patterns
Anomaly/behavior-based detection that flags deviations from a baseline

explanation.correct: Anomaly/behavior-based detection compares activity to a learned baseline, so it can flag novel attacks that have no existing signature (at the cost of more false positives).

distractors.A: A static IP blocklist cannot detect a new attack from an unknown source.
distractors.B: Signature-based detection only catches attacks whose patterns are already known.
distractors.D: A password policy is a preventive control, not a detection method.

explanation.exam_pattern: Known patterns = signature-based; unknown/zero-day via baseline deviation = anomaly/behavior-based.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — IDS detection methods

questions.stem: Which activity BEST demonstrates whether an identified vulnerability can actually be exploited to compromise a system?

options.text: An authorized penetration test that attempts to exploit the weakness
An automated vulnerability scan that lists potential weaknesses
A review of the security policy document

explanation.correct: A penetration test attempts actual exploitation (with authorization), demonstrating whether a weakness is truly exploitable and its real impact.

distractors.A: A survey measures perception, not exploitability.
distractors.C: A vulnerability scan identifies potential weaknesses but does not confirm exploitability.
distractors.D: A policy review assesses documentation, not technical exploitability.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scan = find potential weaknesses (broad); pen test = prove exploitability (depth), with authorization.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Vulnerability scanning vs. penetration testing

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY purpose of maintaining an audit trail of user and system activity?

options.text: To establish individual accountability and enable reconstruction of events
To speed up application response time
To replace the need for access controls

explanation.correct: An audit trail records who did what and when, establishing accountability and letting investigators reconstruct the sequence of events.

distractors.B: Audit logging does not improve application performance.
distractors.C: Audit trails complement, not replace, access controls.
distractors.D: Audit trails consume storage rather than reduce it.

explanation.exam_pattern: Audit trail = accountability (who did what, when) + ability to reconstruct events.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Audit trails and accountability

questions.stem: Why must a data center's HVAC system control HUMIDITY within a defined range?

options.text: Low humidity increases static electricity (ESD) that can damage components, while high humidity causes condensation and corrosion
Humidity sets the server's IP addressing
Humidity changes the strength of the data's encryption

explanation.correct: Humidity that is too low invites static discharge (ESD) that harms electronics, while humidity that is too high promotes condensation and corrosion - both must be avoided.

distractors.B: Humidity is unrelated to IP addressing.
distractors.C: Humidity is unrelated to licensing.
distractors.D: Humidity has no effect on encryption strength.

explanation.exam_pattern: Keep humidity in range - too low = static/ESD, too high = condensation/corrosion.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Environmental controls (HVAC/humidity)

questions.stem: Which water-based fire-suppression system keeps the pipes DRY until a fire is detected, reducing the risk of accidental water damage to equipment, and is therefore often preferred in data centers?

options.text: An open bucket of water at each rack
A wet-pipe sprinkler system that always holds water in the pipes
A deluge system that floods all heads immediately

explanation.correct: A pre-action system holds water back until a detector triggers (and a sprinkler head opens), minimizing the chance of accidental water release over electronics.

distractors.A: A bucket of water is not a suppression system and harms electronics.
distractors.B: A wet-pipe system keeps water in the pipes, risking leaks over equipment.
distractors.D: A deluge system discharges from all heads at once - inappropriate over electronics.

explanation.exam_pattern: Pipes stay dry until detection (then charge, then discharge) = pre-action; preferred where water + electronics coexist.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Fire suppression (pre-action systems)

questions.stem: A UPS keeps systems running for a few minutes during an outage. What is required to sustain operations through a PROLONGED power outage?

options.text: Additional UPS batteries for a few more minutes

explanation.correct: A UPS only bridges short gaps; a backup generator supplies power for the duration of a prolonged outage once it starts and takes over from the UPS.

distractors.B: Cable thickness does not supply power during an outage.
distractors.C: A surge protector conditions power spikes; it provides no power during an outage.
distractors.D: More UPS batteries still only extend short-term runtime.

explanation.exam_pattern: UPS bridges short outages/allows transfer; a generator sustains power through prolonged outages.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Power continuity (UPS vs. generator)

questions.stem: Halon fire-suppression agents were phased out and replaced by clean agents such as FM-200 or inert gases PRIMARILY because Halon:

options.text: Depletes the ozone layer and was restricted under international agreement

explanation.correct: Halon production was banned because it is ozone-depleting (Montreal Protocol); clean agents like FM-200, Novec 1230, and inert gases are the environmentally acceptable replacements.

distractors.A: The driver was environmental impact, not manufacturing cost.
distractors.B: Halon is a fire suppressant, not flammable.
distractors.D: Cabling corrosion was not the reason for phasing out Halon.

explanation.exam_pattern: Halon was banned for ozone depletion -> replaced by clean agents (FM-200, Novec 1230, inert gas).

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Fire suppression agents (Halon replacement)

questions.stem: Which physical security control provides a DETECTIVE record of who entered the data center and when?

options.text: Badge-reader access logs and CCTV recordings

explanation.correct: Badge-reader logs and CCTV recordings capture who entered and when, providing an after-the-fact detective record for review and investigation.

distractors.B: A fence is a preventive/physical barrier, not a record of entries.
distractors.C: A locked door is a preventive control; it keeps people out but keeps no record.
distractors.D: A warning sign is a deterrent and records nothing.

explanation.exam_pattern: Record of who/when entered = access logs/CCTV (detective); locks/fences prevent, signs deter.

references: ISACA CISA Review Manual: Domain 5 — Physical access monitoring
